The Car:  2000 Chevrolet Impala with less than 188,000 miles, V6 3.4 liter engine, automatic transmission, white exterior, gray interior. See window sticker for more details. Three owners since new: the original owner, my mother, and me. Overall this is a nice, clean car. However, it may need a new head gasket (more on this below). Otherwise the car still starts and runs. It was my daily driver until about six months ago. I’m selling it now only because I have too many vehicles and no longer need this one.   The Good:   New parts within the past 2 - 3 years: battery, starter, battery cables, spark plugs, spark plug wires, water pump, thermostat, radiator flush, anti-freeze/coolant, A/C bearing, serpentine belt, front disc brake pads. Tires are in very good condition. Gets about 25 MPG combined city and highway. No known wrecks (it was bumped once in the rear bumper). Other than a few stains (see below), this is a very clean car inside and out. Sale includes a 3-volume set of GM Dealer service manuals and most of the parts and service records since December, 2000.  The Bad:   The engine may need a new head gasket. Although it doesn’t overheat and doesn’t smoke, the engine will occasionally stall; it still runs when it stalls but feels like it may have water in the gas and looses power. The air conditioner does not work (don’t know what the problem is, may just need refrigerant). Fuel gauge does not work (common defect with some GM vehicles of this era). The “Low Coolant Level” dash light comes on/goes off randomly, even if the coolant level is topped off. The “Check Engine” dash light comes on/goes off randomly.  The Ugly:  There are two cracks in the windshield. The paint is peeling and flaking in some areas (another common defect with some GM vehicles of this era). The carpet has a few light stains. There is one place in the carpet beneath the emergency brake that shows heavy wear and tear. And there are some stains in the middle section of the back seat (yes, each of my kids had a “drinking problem” when they were in booster seats).   $1100 cash only. NO trades. 1967 Olds Oldsmobile 442 W30 So cool a must see............ odometer: 32086 1967 Stunning Rare car A 1967 Oldsmobile 2 door sedan 442 W-30 Cutlass ---------------------------------------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Early history information regarding my  Black on Black Beauty! 1967 Oldsmobile 442-W31 SN338077M279104.  To whom it may concern.  This vehicle was specially built for Richard E Haas to campaign in major NHRA drag racing events in 1967. It was important to Oldsmobile， that they had good representation at all regional and national events in an effort to win the NHRA manufacturer's championship.  Oldsmobile won several back-to-back stock car manufacturer's championships during this era.  Dale Smith“Oldsmobile Special Vehicle Operations Manager" was very successful in working with the sanctioning bodies and all types of racers. Dale was able to get a large return for a very small investment(Oldsmobile had no racing budget at this time); Dale was limited to giving a few parts and information to those who chose to run Oldsmobile vehicles.  I worked at the GM Proving Grounds for Oldsmobile， and in1965 ran a 442 automatic. In 1966 I ran a four-speed tri-power and got a little engine help from Mr. Smith. As a GM employee，, I could order and buy a new vehicle equipped， as I wanted at a GM discount. l also had the option of purchasing a vehicle with 3000 miles on it for a larger discount. This 1965 Pontaic GTO is quite possibly the most published  show car in the US. This car has been always stored in a climate controlled garage since built.   In the driveline, backing up the power of the 421 is a Hays clutch, pressure plate and flywheel package.  Capable of handling all of the power that the Big Chief is capable of producing, combined with low pedal effort, the Hays clutch really demonstrates how far technology in this area has come since the thrilling days of yesteryear when the mark of a high performance  was how strong your left leg had to be to depress the clutch pedal!  And backing up the clutch is a Hurst 4-speed equipped Muncie M20 transmission augmented with a Gear Vendors Overdrive.  With a 22% overdrive, The Great One will never breathe hard, even at sustained “high”way speeds, while delivering over 20 mpg!  VEHICLE DESIGN THE GREAT ONE STYLE  Classic design is one of the hallmarks of the GTO, and the Return of The Great One has been carefully restored to maintain its timeless original appearance.  In doing so, we have made only the most subtle visual changes, creating a vehicle that is loaded with “treats.”   While the uninitiated may overlook some of these nuances, true aficionados will find this GTO teeming numerous detail improvements that mark the Return of The Great One as a vehicle that is not only true to the era from which it came, but one that incorporates many of the latest improvements, making it as contemporary and relevant today as when it debuted.  A prime example of this philosophy is the paint.  Inspired by the Hurst Gold of the era, the rarely seen original “Tiger Gold” lacquer was first offered as an option late in the 1965 model year.  The brilliant Sherwin-Williams Planet Color “Hurst Gold” on the Return of The Great One is a modern interpretation of the original, and is the perfect   showcase for the latest in paint technology.    The subtle enhancements continue with the choice of period correct Grand Prix fog lamps mounted in the grille, a distinctive detail that showcases a Pontiac character trait that merges tradition with individuality. Other items to look for are the classic “exhaust splitters” that are attached to a larger than stock diameter exhaust system by Magnaflow, further enhancing the performance  of  the  vehicle,  while  Hotchkis  Performance  has engineered the suspension of the Great One so that it is lower than its stock counterpart.  The result is superlative handling, coupled with a more aggressive appearance and is the perfect complement to the Rally I wheels that contribute to the traditional theme to the vehicle in conjunction with modern BF Goodrich Radial T/A tires.  The Return of the Great One offers the unbridled thrill of a modern high performance vehicle; albeit one that wears the body armor of a highly revered and decorated warrior.  Whether one interprets the name to relate to its spirited high performance, its bold appearance, or the integrated interior, the Return of The Great One definitely has “the right stuff.”  The interior mirrors the theme of that runs throughout The Return of The Great One.  It features seats with magnificent Katzkin hand sewn Parchment Pearl Leather, with stitching that remains true to the original “off the shoulder” pattern.  Contrasting with the leather interior, Tiger Gold Pearl interior surfaces result in a harmony of classic inspired textures and colors.       NAMING THE GREAT ONE    The name of a vehicle is, in many ways, the key to its identity.  We celebrate the GTO with its name.  While it has been known throughout the years by such endearing names as the “Tiger,” the “Goat” and the “GeeTO,” by far, the most revered name has been “The Great One.”  We pay homage to this legendary icon by remaining true to its pedigree and have chosen its most triumphant name.  This vehicle truly marks the Return of The Great One.  CONCLUSION  The Return of The Great One is a classic muscle car that showcases the harmony of vintage and modern components, with performance the equal of a contemporary peer.

The second generation of Corvettes (63-67), also dubbed the Mid-years was in full swing, but soon, it became evident that the 327 CI engine did not offer enough displacement to achieve more power... Say no more, said GM, we got you covered.  The 1965 model offered the first Big Block engine, the L78, 396 CI engine was offered rated at 425 HP.  This Corvette appears to have been born with this engine according to the tell-tale signs, but now it features even more displacement being endowed with a 502 CI engine, a base HO with GM ZZ aluminum heads.  Has MSD transistorized ignition, new fan, polished intake...  Also it has manually operated fuel pump and push-button start, likely putting out close to 500HP, but it was not dyno-ed.  It breathes out via factory look-alike side exhaust. Transmission is a stock 4-speed manual. The engine compartment is highly detailed.    Paint is exquisite and features a deep shine, plenty of clear coating and is virtually flawless.  Car was born "Glen Green", however the actual paint color is a bit darker than the factory one. Lines on the car are beautifully aligned and indicate an unmolested and likely low miler car.  Chrome looks like new, headlights work as they should.  Has nice knock-off wheels running on Cooper Cobra tires.     Undercarriage is extremely clean, correct and presenting very well.  According to the seller, car lived in CA for a long time, thus the "time capsule" look.  Interior is all fresh and correct for the year.  All gauges and instruments are functional, except clock (of course!).  Car is a joy to drive!  It has no power options and, once it warms up, it is a beast!    Beautiful representative example of the era, very hard to duplicate for the money.  The purists may cringe a little bit at the color change, the NOM 502, but hey, check out how "pretty" she is!

Do you want the coolest 4 door from 1970? Do you want a car that has better part availability than most cars on the road today? Do you want a car that will get the attention of everyone young and old?  Well then you are in luck because I have just the car for you!   This is my 1970 Chevy Nova and I would like to put you behind the wheel of it. This Nova is quite the base model as it was ordered with almost no options from the factory. Is that rare? Maybe. Is that desirable? That's up for you to decide. Manual steering, manual brakes, no radio from the factory, crank windows (not even sure if power was an option for these), no passenger mirror, no AC, 3 on the tree transmission, bench seats, and cloth seats. It does however have the juicy 307 small block.  It's a 1970, ya know the most desirable generation of Nova. The generation with the most part availability. The generation that will hold it's value harder than any other generation Nova. You want a two door Nova in this condition? Well have fun paying nearly double.  It's a absolute blast to drive and I ideally don't want to get rid of it but I simply do not have the space for it. I bought it a few weeks ago out near Pueblo, Colorado. The car has spent it's entire life within 100 miles of that town. The previous owner (2nd owner) bought it a few years ago and just did everything in his power to make it a good driver. When I purchased the Nova from him I drove it home over 1,400 miles and ya wanna know how many problems this car gave me? ZERO  I would do the trip again without thinking twice. Not only that, but I did some work to the car once I brought it home such as new spark plugs, valve cover gaskets, belt, battery, breather, air filter, oil change, new tires, and probably some more minor things I forgot to mention.  The Good: Plenty new parts Part availability Cool factor Reliability From a dry climate  The Bad: Only one slightly annoying thing with this car, and that is how the transmission linkage likes to get stuck sometimes in neutral. All ya gotta do is wiggle the shifter a bit and it comes loose again. In over 1400 miles of driving I had it happen 3 times and each time it was easy to get going again. Also the aftermarket radio doesn't work.  The Ugly: As you can see from my images, this car could use some new paint. The clearcoat is fading in some spots, paint is cracking in some areas, and the most minor surface rust imaginable. No major rot or rust anywhere on this car including the underside. I have tried my best to document all the bad spots.  Not sure if it is ugly but I will put it in this category anyway, the hood ornament. Obviously that is not factory but the original owner put it on the car many years ago. I don't think it looks awful so I didn't bother removing it. Also there are some fender skirts in the trunk which I imagine would look awful on this thing.  The other ugly thing is the mirrors. As you can see, it has none. It came with only the driverside mirror and I didn't like how it was mounted (someone mounted it weird) so I took it off and was gonna give it a funky look by giving it fender mounted mirrors. I removed the mirror and bondo'd the holes (didn't sand the bondo yet) but I did not drill into the fenders for the fender mounted mirrors yet so it is still clean. Wanna replace the driver side mirror? Go for it, just gotta sand the bondo down and re-drill the holes.   That's the Nova. I'm asking $10,000 or best offer.
